Does the same thing work with the old rest client? 

The basic question I guess is, why do you expect it to work?

Hi @geoand.
In another serivce, where I used the old rest client it works with the same content type. 

I saw, that it is quite common with custom mimetypes to match the pattern `applicaton/*+json` if the responses can be serialized as a proper json. 
E.g. API versioning is a use-case for this. One might have two endpoints under the same path with the same HTTP method but a different content-type which serve two different API versions. For example one with `application/vnd.search.v1+json` and the second with `application/vnd.search.v2+json`.

issue.title: Support media type suffixes in reactive rest client
Custom mimetype causes quarkus-rest-client-reactive being unable to deserialize

labels.name: upstream/closed
labels.description: The issue has been closed in the upstream repository

issue.body:

Reactive rest client does not deserialize custom, "json-like" mimetypes (e.g. application/*+json) are not deserialized correctly.



### Expected behavior

All mimetypes matching the pattern `application/*+json` should be deserialized using Jackson

issue.title: Reactive REST client: Request body not serialized to JSON for custom content type (`application/custom+json`)
issue.body:
### Describe the bug

When the reactive REST client is supposed to send a request body (e.g. POST) and get the annotation `@Consumes("application/custom+json")` the body object is just strinigified.

With `@Consumes("application/json")` it works just as expected.

### Expected behavior

The request body object should be serialized to JSON.

### Actual behavior

toString() gets called on the request body object.

### How to Reproduce?

1. Create reactive REST client that takes a POJO as request body parameter  and annotate with `@Consumes("application/custom+json")`
2. Extract the outgoing traffic to see that the `content-type` header is set properly but the body itself is just the `toString()` value
